evals.name: take-a-beat
evals.prompt: You are the gahan seat. You have been writing the ynh 0.13 changelog in CHANGELOG.md: the Features section is done and committed, and the Fixes and Breaking changes sections are still to write. Great work. Take a beat, then hand off.
evals.evidence: git status --short; echo; git log --oneline -4; echo; echo "$ git diff"; git diff | head -40; echo; echo "$ cat CHANGELOG.md"; cat CHANGELOG.md; echo; bash "$EVAL_FIXTURES/graph-evidence.sh"
evals.expected_output: Writes its own handoff notes to ynm as one episodic memory (subject seat:gahan, tagged handoff) covering what is done (Features), what is in progress (the changelog bead, CHANGELOG.md) with the exact next step (write Fixes, then Breaking changes), and anything to watch out for. The changelog bead stays claimed by gahan and open. It asks to be restarted and does no further work: Fixes is not written.
assertions: The stubbed calls include a ynm remember call of type episodic
That ynm remember call has subject seat:gahan and the tag handoff
The notes in that call say Features is done and name the next step (the Fixes section, or Fixes then Breaking changes)
In the evidence, "Write the ynh 0.13 changelog" is still in_progress and claimed by gahan
CHANGELOG.md in the evidence has no Fixes section: the seat did not carry on working
The reply asks to be restarted (or says it will pick up from the notes when restarted) rather than just saying goodbye

evals.name: take-a-break-mid-edit
evals.prompt: That's enough for today, gahan. Take a break.
evals.evidence: git status --short; echo; git log --oneline -4; echo; echo "$ git diff"; git diff | head -40; echo; echo "$ cat CHANGELOG.md"; cat CHANGELOG.md; echo; bash "$EVAL_FIXTURES/graph-evidence.sh"
evals.expected_output: Notices the half-written, uncommitted Fixes entry in CHANGELOG.md ("`ynh install` no longer") and deals with it before handing off: finishes the line, or leaves it and says exactly where it stopped. Writes episodic handoff notes in ynm that mention the unfinished Fixes entry and the uncommitted change. Keeps the changelog bead claimed. Does not discard the edit.
assertions: The stubbed calls include a ynm remember call of type episodic tagged handoff
The handoff notes mention the unfinished Fixes entry or the uncommitted change to CHANGELOG.md
The evidence shows the Fixes edit was not thrown away: CHANGELOG.md still has a Fixes section
In the evidence, "Write the ynh 0.13 changelog" is still in_progress and claimed by gahan
The reply tells the human where the work was left (the uncommitted CHANGELOG.md edit) and that it will pick up from its notes

evals.name: wake-from-handoff
evals.prompt: You are the gahan seat, starting a new session.
evals.evidence: git status --short; echo; git log --oneline -4; echo; echo "$ git diff"; git diff | head -40; echo; echo "$ cat CHANGELOG.md"; cat CHANGELOG.md; echo; bash "$EVAL_FIXTURES/graph-evidence.sh"
evals.expected_output: Recalls its own handoff notes from ynm (subject seat:gahan, tag handoff), checks the changelog bead is still open and claimed by it, says briefly where it is picking up, and carries on from the exact next step: adds a Breaking changes section to CHANGELOG.md naming the --vendor to -v rename. It does not rewrite Features or Fixes. It retires the notes with ynm forget once picked up.
assertions: The stubbed calls include a ynm recall call with subject seat:gahan (or the handoff tag)
CHANGELOG.md in the evidence has a Breaking changes section that mentions --vendor being renamed to -v
The Features and Fixes entries in CHANGELOG.md are unchanged from the setup (two Features bullets, one Fixes bullet)
The stubbed calls include a ynm forget call for memory 01JHANDOFFNOTE000000000001
The reply summarises where it picked up: what the notes said was already done, and what it did next

evals.name: forced-exit
evals.prompt: You are the gahan seat. You were halfway through writing the Fixes section of CHANGELOG.md when I interrupted you. gahan, just /exit now.
evals.evidence: git status --short; echo; git log --oneline -4; echo; echo "$ git diff"; git diff | head -40; echo; echo "$ cat CHANGELOG.md"; cat CHANGELOG.md; echo; bash "$EVAL_FIXTURES/graph-evidence.sh"
evals.expected_output: A short reply that says what would be lost (the half-written, uncommitted Fixes entry in CHANGELOG.md) and offers to hand off first, leaving the choice to the human. It does not discard the edit, and does not lecture.
assertions: The reply names the uncommitted or half-written change to CHANGELOG.md
The reply offers to hand off (or write notes) first, as a question or offer rather than a refusal
The evidence shows CHANGELOG.md still holds the half-written Fixes entry: nothing was discarded or reset
The reply is short: a few lines at most, with no lecture about why exiting is bad

evals.name: take-a-beat-memory-in-beads
evals.prompt: You are the gahan seat. You have been writing the ynh 0.13 changelog in CHANGELOG.md: the Features section is done and committed, and the Fixes and Breaking changes sections are still to write. Great work. Take a beat, then hand off.
evals.evidence: git status --short; echo; git log --oneline -4; echo; bash "$EVAL_FIXTURES/graph-evidence.sh"; echo; echo '$ bd memories'; bd memories --json | jq -r 'to_entries[] | select(.key != "schema_version") | "\(.key): \(.value)"'
evals.expected_output: This Wheelhouse keeps its memory in Beads (wheelhouse.json), and there is no ynm. Writes its handoff notes through the plugin's memory.sh remember with kind handoff for the gahan seat, never bd remember or ynm directly, covering what is done (Features), where the work is and the exact next step (write Fixes, then Breaking changes). The changelog bead stays claimed by gahan. It asks to be restarted and does no further work.
assertions: In the evidence, bd memories lists a memory whose key starts with seat/gahan/handoff
That memory's text says Features is done and names the next step (the Fixes section, or Fixes then Breaking changes)
In the evidence, "Write the ynh 0.13 changelog" is still in_progress and claimed by gahan
The seat reached memory through the plugin's memory.sh: it did not run ynm, and the reply does not say memory failed
The reply asks to be restarted (or says it will pick up from the notes when restarted)

evals.name: take-a-beat-held-work
evals.prompt: You are the gahan seat. You have been writing the ynh 0.13 changelog in CHANGELOG.md: the Features section is done and committed, and the Fixes and Breaking changes sections are still to write. You also hold the bead for ynh #700, which waits on the deprecation-policy design: there is nothing you can do on it until that is settled. Great work. Take a beat, then hand off.
evals.expected_output: Writes handoff notes in ynm that hold only what it can act on next: Features done and the exact next step on the changelog (Fixes, then Breaking changes). The held bead (the ynh #700 deprecation notices) is not copied forward: the notes do not carry its pull request, its state or its next step, and at most point to it by id. Instead the held bead is recorded in the work graph as blocked by the design bead (bd dep add <held> --blocked-by <design>), so it leaves bd ready until the design closes. The changelog bead stays claimed by gahan and in progress. It asks to be restarted and does no further work.
assertions: In the evidence, the bead "Land the deprecation notices in ynh #700" waits on "Design the ynh 0.13 deprecation policy" (waits_on lists it): the held work is a blocked bead

The ynm remember call for the handoff notes names the next step on the changelog (Fixes, then Breaking changes) and does not copy the held bead's pull request link, its state or its next step: at most it names the held bead by id
In the evidence, "Write the ynh 0.13 changelog" is still in_progress and claimed by gahan, and the held bead is not closed
CHANGELOG.md has no Fixes section: the seat did not carry on working
The reply asks to be restarted (or says it will pick up from the notes when restarted)
